theater: 高加索伊比利亞與庫拉河谷

battle.name: 伊比利亞戰爭
battle.theater: 高加索伊比利亞與庫拉河谷
battle.brief: 526年薩珊沙赫卡瓦德一世企圖完全控制高加索伊比利亞王國，伊比利亞貴族向君士坦丁堡求援，拜占庭遠征軍與波斯騎兵在提比里斯、庫拉河谷及多摩山口拉鋸六年，卡瓦德532年被弒後雙方休戰。卡面羅馬方陣盾早已停產，但其盾緣咬合的方陣紀律仍以魚骨陣形式留在拜占庭步兵手上。

kit.name: 羅馬方陣盾
kit.history: 凸面的長方盾。羅馬的防線靠盾緣咬住盾緣，不是靠盾牌多厚。

countries: 東羅馬（拜占庭）帝國一方以君士坦丁堡為中樞，查士丁尼一世527年即位後親自決定高加索戰區的用兵；野戰指揮分給「東方軍區總督」與數名各自帶兵的將領，靠祕書、軍需官與信使維持上下互通。聯盟範圍遠出帝國邊疆：高加索的伊比利亞王國（卡爾特利）提供地面基地，紅海西岸的阿克蘇姆王國出錢出船，阿拉伯沙漠的加薩尼人牽制薩珊南方，黑海北岸與北高加索的匈奴、赫魯利人供應外族兵員，亞美尼亞人瓦漢所部則由君士坦丁堡發餉。薩珊波斯一方以泰西封為都，沙赫卡瓦德一世在位（459–532），北方邊防由總督與軍團長分轄，投入的是薩珊中央直轄的野戰軍與北方草原的拉赫姆人、薩比爾人部眾，並在伊比利亞扶植傀儡政權與守軍。戰場在高加索主脈南麓、庫拉河上游的伊比利亞盆地：北面只有多摩山口一條低隘通道通阿蘭草原，西北可經黑海港口回君士坦丁堡，東南沿山道可達波斯治下的亞美尼亞與拉奇。一條河谷、幾座山口，就是這場戰爭全部的地理。
countriesEn: The Byzantine side was organised from Constantinople, with Emperor Justinian I taking personal charge of the Caucasian theatre after his accession in 527. Field command was divided between the magister militum per Orientem and several generals operating with independent detachments, tied together by a network of scribes, logisticians and couriers. Its coalition reached far beyond the imperial frontier: the Kingdom of Iberia in the Caucasus, in Kartli, supplied the land base, the Aksumite kingdom across the Red Sea supplied money and shipping, the Ghassanids of the Arabian desert tied down the Sasanians in the south, Huns and Heruli from the northern Black Sea littoral and the North Caucasian steppe provided foreign troops, and the Armenian contingent under Vahan was paid out of Constantinople. The Sasanian side worked from Ctesiphon under Shah Kavad I, reigned from 459 to 532, with the northern frontier divided among governors and military commanders; it committed the central army of the Sasanians themselves together with steppe peoples such as the Lakhmids and Sabirs, and propped up a dependent regime and its garrisons inside Iberia. The battlefield lay in the upper Kura valley of Iberia, a basin on the southern foot of the main Caucasus range: to the north the Darial pass was the single low defile leading to the Alan steppe, to the north-west the Black Sea ports led back toward Constantinople, to the south-east the mountain tracks ran down to Sasanian Armenia and Lazica. One river valley and a few passes were the whole geography of this war.
people: 卡瓦德一世（Kavad I）是發動戰爭的決策者，這位薩珊沙赫在北方與嚈噠交戰、疲於應付之後轉向西北擴張，試圖把伊比利亞完全收進版圖；他在位末年被兒子佩羅茲（Peroz）推翻殺死，532年異鄉死去，這一政變直接改變了戰爭的收場方式。查士丁尼一世（Justinian I）是拜占庭的推手：伊比利亞流亡貴族的使團抵達君士坦丁堡時，他以「東方軍區總督」的身分拍板出兵，並在戰局僵持時批准增援。米赫蘭（Mihran）是密赫拉尼德王族的王子，他與被波斯廢黜的兄弟伊比利亞的佩羅茲先後流亡，藉羅馬的干預重獲王位，是整場衝突的委託人。亞美尼亞人瓦漢（Vahan）是拜占庭在高加索最可靠的將領之一，長期以 spatamen 身分領軍；馬爾提努斯（Martinus）負責亞美尼亞與阿布哈吉亞方向；布澤斯（Buzes）原是薩珊的亞美尼亞籍官員，叛投後替拜占庭引導高加索的戰役節奏。波斯方面，米爾達特（Mirdat）是受命進入伊比利亞的主將，531年的決定性戰役中他被擊敗並全軍覆沒；拉赫姆人與赫魯利人的首領則分別在阿拉伯與黑海兩端拉開戰線。留下記載的有馬拉拉斯與普羅科匹烏斯，後者描述的魚骨陣與遠征細節，是我們理解當時布陣的主要依據。
peopleEn: Kavad I was the man who decided to start the war. The Sasanian shah, exhausted by long fighting against the Hephthalites in the north, turned to expand towards the north-west and to fold Iberia completely into the empire; at the end of his reign his own son Peroz overthrew and killed him, and he died in 532, and that putsch directly changed the way the war closed. Justinian I was the Byzantine engine of it: when the embassy of the Iberian exiles reached Constantinople he decided to send an expedition in his capacity as magister militum per Orientem, and he approved reinforcements when the front stalled. Mihran, a prince of the Mihranid house, and his deposed brother Peroz of Iberia went into exile one after another and regained their position through Roman intervention, and they were the clients who asked for the whole war. The Armenian Vahan was one of the most reliable Byzantine commanders in the Caucasus, serving for years as a spatamen; Martinus handled the Armenian and Abasgian fronts, and Buzes, an Armenian-born official of the Sasanian state who had changed sides, guided the tempo of the Caucasian campaigns for Constantinople. On the Persian side Mirdat was the commander sent into Iberia; he was defeated and his army destroyed in the decisive engagement of 531, while the chiefs of the Lakhmids and of the Heruli opened fronts at the opposite ends of the empire, in Arabia and on the Black Sea. Malalas and Procopius left the narrative, and Procopius, who describes the cheindon and the marches in detail, remains the principal source for the order of battle of that moment.
kits: 卡面的羅馬方陣盾（scutum）是共和國末期至帝國初期軍團的標誌：凸面長方，左右兩列扣在盾緣上，羅馬人靠盾牆而不是靠盾牌厚度取勝。但到526年，這種盾早已停產數百年，晚期羅馬軍改成平凸的橢圓大盾與小圓盾，五至六世紀的東羅馬重步兵裝備的是扁平橢圓盾，輕裝步兵用小圓盾（拉丁文 scutum 後來反而指小圓盾）；普羅科匹烏斯記載的魚骨陣 cheindon——士兵以盾相接、槍尖越肩而列——正是一種方陣盾的變形，說明羅馬以盾緣咬合的紀律仍然活著。波斯方面，步兵 spah-rizak 以小型圓盾配弓與短矛，弓箭手上弦不需大盾，重騎兵 savaran 用長矛與薩珊複合弓，不帶大盾護身；薩珊弓短而反曲，適合騎射，缺的正是羅馬式密集盾牆的緩衝。雙方遠征軍都靠馱獸隊輸送糧秣與箭壺，攻守城塞時用撞錘與攻城塔；高加索考古也證實邊軍沿用羅馬裝備體系，阿布哈吉亞的阿普薩羅斯要塞出土大批羅馬分段甲殘件，正是六世紀拜占庭守軍所佩。
kitsEn: The scutum on the card is a badge of the Roman army of the late Republic and early Empire: a convex rectangle whose two files hooked edge to edge, so that Rome won by a wall of shields rather than by the thickness of any single shield. By 526 that shield had been out of production for centuries. The late Roman army had moved on to the flat oval shield and the small round one, and the fifth and sixth century Eastern Roman heavy infantry carried flat oval shields while light troops carried small round bucklers, the Latin word scutum by then actually denoting the small round shield. The cheindon, the fishbone formation described by Procopius, in which men lock shields together and hold spears over the shoulder, is a direct descendant of that scutum discipline and shows that the Roman practice of biting shield edge into shield edge was still alive. On the Persian side the infantry, the spah-rizak, carried small round shields with bow and short spear, archers shot without any shield at all, and the heavy cavalry, the savaran, used lance and the Sasanian composite bow and wore no large shield for protection; the Persian bow was short and strongly recurved, made for shooting from horseback, and what the Persians lacked was the buffering quality of a dense Roman shield wall. Both sides moved their expeditionary armies on pack animals carrying grain and arrow jars, and used rams and siege towers against the fortresses; archaeology on the Caucasian side confirms that the frontier troops still used Roman equipment, since the fortress of Apsaros in Abkhazia has yielded a large number of Roman lorica segmentata plates, the actual kit of sixth century Byzantine garrisons.
tactics: 拜占庭的戰法是把決戰押在城塞與隘道，而不是押在曠野：野戰部隊沿庫拉河谷與山道推進時以投射武器齊射與盾牆自保，重騎兵擔任反擊與追擊，步兵在接戰前列成魚骨陣，用盾緣咬住、以長矛頂住薩珊的衝鋒，隨後再以小股騎兵反覆襲擾敵軍側翼與糧道；將領寧願拖延、封鎖山口、等波斯遠離其補給縱深，也不願在無遮蔽的高原上決戰。戰爭同時在多條戰線展開，加薩尼人在沙漠咬住拉赫姆人、匈奴與赫魯利人威脅北線、阿克蘇姆的船隊監視紅海，等於把薩珊的兵員與注意力分散到三個方向，讓高加索戰線得以長期維持。薩珊則完全相反：以弓騎為主力的快速縱深突進，沿庫拉河谷直插伊比利亞首府提比里斯，兵鋒穿過險隘時以重騎兵和攏兵掩護突擊兵，抵達後立刻改為圍城與斷糧，逼拜占庭遠征軍在補給拉長時作出取捨。冬季的高加索山道是薩珊的優勢，也是雙方補給線的瓶頸，誰控制山口與渡口，誰就決定戰役節奏。
tacticsEn: Byzantine practice was to keep the decision in the fortresses and the passes rather than in the open field. Columns moving along the Kura valley and the mountain tracks covered themselves with volleys of missile troops and with the shield wall; the cavalry were held back for counter-stroke and pursuit; infantry formed the cheindon before contact, locking shield edge and meeting the Persian charge with long spears; and small bodies of horse were then sent repeatedly against the enemy flank and supply lines. The generals preferred to wait, to close the passes and to let the Persians move away from their line of supply, rather than to fight a general action on a bare plateau. The war was fought on several fronts at once, with the Ghassanids biting the Lakhmids in the desert, Huns and Heruli threatening the northern line and Aksumite squadrons watching the Red Sea, which divided Sasanian troops and attention three ways and allowed the Caucasian front to be sustained. Sasanian method was the exact opposite: fast deep penetration by mounted archers straight down the Kura valley toward the Iberian capital at Tbilisi; when a column forced a defile, heavy cavalry and lancers covered the assault; on arrival they switched at once to siege and to cutting supply, forcing the Byzantine expedition to choose as its line of supply lengthened. The Caucasian winter favoured the Persians and was at the same time the bottleneck of both supply lines; whoever held the passes and the fords set the rhythm of the campaign.
data: 可核對的只有框架數字：戰爭自526年伊比利亞使團抵達君士坦丁堡起，到532年卡瓦德被弒、雙方達成休戰為止，前後約六年，真正的高強度交會集中在527至531年。拜占庭先後派出的遠征軍在編年史中被描述為數千人至一萬餘人，具體名冊已不可考；波斯方面的遠征軍則被記為人數眾多，通常以萬計估計。531年的決定性戰役中，波斯主將陣亡、部隊被大量俘虜，這是雙方文獻唯一沒有爭議的損失紀錄。地理上，黑海港口皮提烏斯到提比里斯約三百至四百公里，山道行軍按日計，冬季封山會把補給拖成以月計的難題。日期方面可確定者有526年使團抵達、527年查士丁尼即位與出兵、531年會戰、532年佩羅茲弒父並與拜占庭簽訂休戰；至於開戰的確切月份，史料並無記載，只能依高加索春季開河的季節規律推為四月。
dataEn: Only the frame of the numbers survives. The war runs from 526, when the Iberian embassy reached Constantinople, to 532, when Kavad was killed and the two sides came to terms, about six years in all, with the heavy fighting concentrated between 527 and 531. Byzantine chronicles describe the expeditionary armies sent out as numbering from several thousand to something over ten thousand, and the roster no longer exists; the Persian invading force is recorded as numerous and is generally estimated in tens of thousands. In the decisive engagement of 531 the Persian commander was killed and his troops were captured in large numbers, and that is the one casualty account on which the two literatures do not differ. Geographically it is about three hundred to four hundred kilometres from the Black Sea port of Pityus to Tbilisi; marching in the mountains was counted by the day, while a winter closure of the passes turned supply into a problem counted in months. The dates that can be fixed are 526 for the embassy, 527 for Justinian's accession and the dispatch of the expedition, 531 for the field battle, and 532 for Peroz's murder of his father and the truce with Byzantium; the exact month of the opening is not recorded at all and can only be inferred from the seasonal regularity of the Caucasian spring thaw, which points to April.
cause: 起因有三層。第一層是薩珊的邊境戰略：卡瓦德一世在北方草原與嚈噠長期消耗，亟需在西北與東北取得戰略縱深，把高加索的山口與裡海方向抓在手中，於是把伊比利亞王國視為必須整頓的藩屬。第二層是伊比利亞內部的王位糾紛：密赫拉尼德家族與波斯扶植的傀儡政權互相猜忌，貴族殺死波斯任命的總督，主權與稅賦爭議全面爆發，王子米赫蘭兄弟被迫流亡。第三層是拜占庭的介入動機：查士丁尼希望把薩珊的兵力黏在高加索，同時在阿拉伯與紅海方向打開缺口，於是對伊比利亞的求援給出超出常規的回應，把一場地方性的叛亂牽成了兩大帝國在高加索的全面對抗。引爆點則是多摩山口與庫拉河谷的推進節奏，一旦波斯騎兵越過山口深入盆地，兩邊就再也沒有退讓的餘地。
causeEn: There are three layers to the cause. The first is Sasanian frontier strategy: Kavad I, worn down by years of attrition against the Hephthalites on the northern steppe, needed strategic depth to the north-west and north-east, wanted the passes of the Caucasus and the direction of the Caspian in his hands, and therefore treated the Kingdom of Iberia as a vassal that had to be reorganised. The second is the succession quarrel inside Iberia: the Mihranid house and the Persian sponsored puppet regime mistrusted each other, nobles killed the Persian appointed governor, the questions of sovereignty and taxation came to a head, and the princes Mihran and his brother were driven into exile. The third is the Byzantine reason for interfering: Justinian wanted to pin Sasanian troops in the Caucasus while opening a gap in Arabia and on the Red Sea, so he answered the Iberian appeal more generously than usual, and what had been a local rebellion became an all out confrontation between the two empires in the Caucasus. The point of ignition was the tempo of movement through the Darial pass and the Kura valley; once Persian horse crossed the passes into the basin, neither side had any room left to give way.
impact: 這場戰爭決定了六世紀高加索的權力格局。拜占庭在伊比利亞扶起密赫拉尼德王朝的附庸政權，取得提比里斯、阿特斯庫里等要塞組成的邊防網，把薩珊的勢力線壓回庫拉河與阿拉加尼河的分水嶺；阿克蘇姆與加薩尼人的牽制則削弱波斯在紅海與阿拉伯的收成。531到532年的戰果讓查士丁尼相信羅馬可以在東線主動出擊，邊防式的保守戰略隨之被放棄，直接通向540年代拉齊卡戰爭那場更漫長、更高消耗的高加索戰役。對伊比利亞王國自身，代價是成為兩強的緩衝地：它在兩位宗主之間反覆搖擺，558年波斯再度扶植傀儡干政，國家長期處於附庸與叛亂交替的循環。對後世而言，這也是東羅馬第一次在高加索建立常態干預的樣本，之後幾個世紀裡拜占庭與薩珊在黑海東岸的所有拉鋸，都可以視為這六年的放大版。
impactEn: This war settled the power pattern of the Caucasus in the sixth century. Byzantium restored a dependent regime of the Mihranid house in Iberia and obtained a chain of frontier strongholds around Tbilisi and Atskuri, pushing the Sasanian line back to the watershed between the Kura and the Alazani; the pressure from Aksum and the Ghassanids cut into Persian revenues in the Red Sea and in Arabia. The victories of 531 and 532 convinced Justinian that Rome could take the initiative in the east, and the defensive patient strategy was dropped, which led directly to the far longer and far more exhausting Lazic War in the 540s. For the Kingdom of Iberia itself the cost was to become a buffer between the two powers, swinging from one master to the other, with a new Persian puppet imposed in 558, so that the country spent long decades alternating between vassalage and revolt. For later ages this was also the first sample of a permanent Byzantine presence in the Caucasus, and every subsequent pull between Byzantium and the Sasanians on the eastern Black Sea littoral can be read as an enlargement of these six years.
result: 沒有任何一方取得決定性的戰果。拜占庭贏了每一場會戰，卻沒有把伊比利亞變成行省，也沒有把軍隊推進到山脈北麓；伊比利亞王國在密赫拉尼德家族手中保持自治，同時向兩個宗主繳納貢賦、徵發兵員。波斯軍隊退出盆地，卻保留在亞美尼亞與拉奇的據點，修復了北線的關隘。532年佩羅茲弒父自立後，與查士丁尼簽下約五年的休戰（達拉條約），戰爭以雙方都還能再打、但都打不贏的狀態收束。實質的結果是一條被拉長的高加索前線、兩套並存的附庸體系，以及一次慘勝之後必然到來的更大規模衝突；二十多年後的拉齊卡戰爭，正是這場伊比利亞戰爭的放大與重演。
resultEn: Neither side won a decisive result. Byzantium won every field engagement, yet did not turn Iberia into a province and did not push its troops past the northern foot of the range; the Kingdom of Iberia kept its autonomy in the hands of the Mihranids while paying tribute and providing contingents to two masters at once. The Persian army withdrew from the basin but kept its positions in Armenia and Lazica and repaired the fortified passes on the northern line. In 532, after Peroz had killed his father and taken the throne, he concluded a truce of about five years with Justinian, the treaty of Dara, and the war closed in a state where both sides could fight again but neither could win outright. The real outcome was a lengthened Caucasian front line, two parallel systems of clientage, and a larger conflict certain to follow a costly victory; the Lazic War more than twenty years later was the enlargement and the repetition of this Iberian war.
